about.title: Sanger Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Sanger sits at the center of a farming economy, and its stores, packing sheds, and public buildings see heavy daily foot traffic from residents and seasonal workers alike. When a wet floor, broken step, or poorly lit walkway causes a fall, the aftermath often means more than a bruise — it can mean missed work and mounting medical costs. California law requires the injured person to show the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. That's why documenting the scene matters: photos of the spill or defect, names of witnesses, and a written incident report can make a real difference later. Surveillance footage from stores along Academy Avenue or Jensen Avenue, for example, is often overwritten within days or weeks, so acting quickly matters. LawProactive doesn't charge anything to connect you with an independent attorney who handles these cases on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Sanger Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding of the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California requires proof that a property owner knew or should have known about a hazard before it caused harm. An attorney can help gather the evidence needed to establish that notice.

items.title: Fast Action to Preserve Evidence
items.desc: Surveillance video and maintenance logs often get deleted or discarded quickly. Connecting with an attorney soon after a fall can help make sure that evidence is requested before it disappears.

items.title: Guidance Through Comparative Fault Rules
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the fall, though your share of fault may reduce the amount recovered.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Sanger?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process. It's worth having an attorney review your situation as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some blame, such as not noticing a posted warning sign. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help evaluate how this might apply to your specific case.

items.question: I fell at a store on Bethel Avenue and no one gave me an incident report. What should I do?
items.answer: Try to write down what happened as soon as you can, including the date, time, and exact location, and take photos of the hazard if it's still possible. Ask for the names of any employees or witnesses present. An independent attorney can help request the store's internal records and any available surveillance footage.
